claims: FISA is the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
FISA is a U.S. federal law.
FISA regulates electronic surveillance and physical searches for foreign intelligence.
FISA establishes the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC).
FISC oversees electronic surveillance and physical searches for foreign intelligence.
FISA requires warrants based on probable cause that targets are foreign powers or their agents.
FISC is a specialized court of federal judges.
FISA covers surveillance, physical searches, and business records acquisition.
Section 702 is a 2008 addition to FISA.
Section 702 allows targeted surveillance of non-U.S. persons located outside the U.S. without individual warrants.
Section 702 often results in incidental collection of Americans' data.
Critics raise concerns about FBI, CIA, and NSA accessing Section 702 data for investigations involving U.S. citizens.
The Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act (RISAA) renewed Section 702 for two years until April 2026.
Short-term extensions were utilized in April 2026 due to resistance over the scope of surveillance.
FISA has been modified by the PATRIOT Act.
FISA has been modified by the USA Freedom Act.
